result.rationale: The diff shows `<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>` — the onOpenChange handler only toggles open state, while the Cancel button explicitly resets `setMultiEmailValue([""])` and `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`. The mutation's onSuccess also resets both. So closing via backdrop/Escape leaves stale `multiEmailValue` and `isInvalidEmail`, and reopening shows the old emails and a lingering red validation error. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the new AddGuestsDialog component.

judged_text: Closing the dialog via Dialog onOpenChange (clicking the backdrop or Escape) resets neither multiEmailValue nor isInvalidEmail, unlike the Cancel button which resets both. A user who triggers the validation error, closes the dialog via backdrop/Escape, and reopens it sees the stale red 'Emails must be unique and valid' error and their previous emails with no way to realize the state wasn't fresh; two close paths have drifted apart.

The only reset logic (`setMultiEmailValue([""])` and `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`) is inside the Cancel button onClick.
